opts.B: That the property will be kept in perfect repair
opts.C: That no improvements may be made to the property during the lease
opts.D: The right to possess and enjoy the property without interference from the landlord or anyone claiming through the landlord

questions.exp: The covenant of quiet enjoyment guarantees the tenant's undisturbed use and possession of the leased property. If the landlord — or anyone with a superior title — interferes with this right (e.g., wrongful entry, third-party eviction), the tenant may have grounds to terminate the lease or claim damages.

questions.q: Constructive eviction occurs when:

opts.A: The landlord's actions (or failure to maintain the property) make the premises uninhabitable, forcing the tenant to leave
opts.B: The landlord gives the tenant a 30-day notice to vacate
opts.C: A court orders the tenant to leave
opts.D: The tenant voluntarily moves out before the lease ends

questions.exp: Constructive eviction occurs when the landlord fails to perform a duty that renders the property unfit for the intended purpose (no heat in winter, persistent flooding, uninhabitable conditions), effectively forcing the tenant to vacate. If successful, the tenant may terminate the lease and sue for damages.

questions.q: Under Pennsylvania's Landlord-Tenant Act, a landlord must return a residential security deposit within how many days after the tenancy ends?

opts.A: 30 days
opts.B: 21 days
opts.C: 15 days
opts.D: 45 days

questions.exp: Pennsylvania's Landlord-Tenant Act (68 P.S. § 250.512) requires landlords to return the security deposit (or provide an itemized written statement of deductions) within 30 days after the tenancy ends and the tenant delivers possession. Failure to comply may result in liability for double the withheld deposit plus attorney's fees.

questions.q: A tenant subletting their apartment to another person (subtenant) remains:

opts.A: Released from all liability to the landlord
opts.B: The landlord's primary tenant only if the sublet is approved
opts.C: Only responsible for their own use of the property
opts.D: Liable to the landlord under the original lease

questions.exp: In a sublease, the original tenant (sublessor) remains directly liable to the landlord under the original lease. The subtenant is responsible to the sublessor. If the subtenant fails to pay rent, the original tenant still owes it to the landlord. An assignment transfers all rights AND primary liability to the assignee.

questions.q: When a landlord sells a property with tenants, the buyer generally:

opts.A: May immediately evict all tenants regardless of lease terms
opts.B: Takes the property subject to existing leases and must honor them
opts.C: Becomes the landlord only after the leases expire
opts.D: Must offer the tenants first right of refusal to purchase

questions.exp: The "sale does not break the lease" principle (embodied in URLTA and most state laws) means a buyer who purchases a rental property takes title subject to existing valid leases. The buyer steps into the seller's shoes as landlord and must honor all lease terms until they lawfully expire.

questions.q: A property management agreement between an owner and a property manager is a(n):

opts.A: Agency agreement establishing the scope of the manager's authority
opts.B: Lease agreement between owner and manager
opts.C: License to occupy the property
opts.D: Sales contract contingent on future performance

questions.exp: A property management agreement is an agency contract that defines the property manager's authority (scope of management), compensation, duties, reporting requirements, and the duration of the management relationship. The manager acts as the owner's agent in managing the property.

questions.q: Under Fair Housing laws, a landlord who refuses to rent to a person because they receive a Section 8 housing voucher is:

opts.A: Permitted under federal Fair Housing Act (source of income is not federally protected)
opts.B: Potentially violating Pennsylvania and local laws that prohibit source of income discrimination
opts.C: Violating only ECOA
opts.D: Protected by the private property exemption to fair housing

questions.exp: Source of income (including housing vouchers) is NOT a protected class under the federal Fair Housing Act. However, Pennsylvania and many local jurisdictions (Philadelphia, Pittsburgh) have added source of income to their local anti-discrimination laws. In those jurisdictions, refusing to rent to a voucher holder may be illegal.

questions.q: A "net operating income" (NOI) of $50,000 and a cap rate of 8% indicates a property value of approximately:
questions.exp: Value = NOI ÷ Cap Rate = $50,000 ÷ 0.08 = $625,000. This is the Income Capitalization Approach: the NOI is divided by the market capitalization rate to estimate the property's market value. A lower cap rate yields a higher value; a higher cap rate yields a lower value.

questions.q: The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requires that newly constructed commercial buildings:

opts.A: Have only ramps on the exterior
opts.B: Be designed and constructed to be fully accessible to persons with disabilities
opts.C: Provide accessible units equivalent to 10% of total units
opts.D: Provide one accessible parking space per 100 spaces

questions.exp: Title III of the ADA requires that all newly constructed commercial facilities and places of public accommodation built for first occupancy after January 26, 1993, be designed and constructed in compliance with ADA accessibility standards — ensuring full accessibility from the start rather than retrofitting.

questions.q: A management fee for a property manager is MOST commonly structured as:

opts.A: A flat monthly fee regardless of collected rent
opts.B: A percentage of gross potential income (whether collected or not)
opts.C: A percentage of actual collected rents
opts.D: A per-unit annual fee multiplied by the number of occupied units

questions.exp: Property management fees for residential properties are most commonly a percentage (typically 8-12%) of actual collected rents. This structure aligns incentives — the manager earns more when rents are collected and occupancy is high, motivating effective management and tenant retention.

questions.q: Which of the following is a landlord's responsibility under the implied warranty of habitability?

opts.A: Maintaining the property in like-new condition at all times
opts.B: Keeping the property in a condition fit for human habitation (adequate heat, plumbing, structural integrity)
opts.C: Providing luxury amenities as described in any advertising
opts.D: Replacing all appliances upon tenant request

questions.exp: The implied warranty of habitability (recognized in Pennsylvania) requires landlords to maintain rental properties in a condition suitable for human habitation — with functional heating, plumbing, electrical systems, weatherproofing, and structural soundness. Tenants may withhold rent, repair and deduct, or terminate the lease if this warranty is breached.
